revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Square Mirrors
revealWordProblem.text:
The side lengths of two square mirrors are shown. Mirror A has sides of 2½ feet and Mirror B has sides of 1¾ feet.
Question: About how many times greater is the area of Mirror A than the area of Mirror B?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Two square mirrors side by side: Mirror A is 2 and one-half feet across and Mirror B is 1 and three-fourths feet across.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Find each area first. Mirror A: 2½ × 2½ = 5/2 × 5/2 = 25/4 = 6¼ square feet. Mirror B: 1¾ × 1¾ = 7/4 × 7/4 = 49/16 = 3 1/16 square feet. Now divide to compare: 25/4 ÷ 49/16 = 25/4 × 16/49 = 400/196 ≈ 2.04. Mirror A's area is about 2 times greater than Mirror B's.

steps: 2. Change the division symbol (÷) to multiplication (×)
3. Flip the second fraction to its reciprocal (d/c), then multiply across and simplify
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Divide Fractions is flipping the wrong fraction: students flip the dividend (the first fraction) instead of the divisor (the second fraction). For example, solving 3/4 ÷ 5/8 by flipping 3/4 to 4/3 and keeping 5/8 gives 4/3 × 5/8 = 20/24 = 5/6 — but only the divisor gets flipped. Keep 3/4, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 5/8 to its reciprocal 8/5: 3/4 × 8/5 = 24/20 = 6/5. Before you submit, check that the fraction you kept (the dividend) is still facing the same way it started.

level3.prompt: Is 3/4 ÷ 1/2 the same as 1/2 ÷ 3/4? Solve both and explain why or why not. What does this tell you about the order in division?
level3.sentenceFrame: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 = ___ and 1/2 ÷ 3/4 = ___. These are ___ because ___. This shows that division is ___.
level3.hint: Explain how dividing by smaller fractions produces larger quotients using a real scenario.
hints: Don't assume the two divisions match — solve each one on its own first.
Use Keep, Change, Flip on both: flip the second fraction each time, then compare the two quotients.
First one: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 → 3/4 × 2/1. Work it out, then set up 1/2 ÷ 3/4 the same way and compare.
level3.explanation: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 becomes 3/4 × 2/1 = 6/4 = 1 1/2, while 1/2 ÷ 3/4 becomes 1/2 × 4/3 = 4/6 = 2/3, so the two expressions are not equal. Swapping the dividend and the divisor flips the quotient to its reciprocal, which shows that division is not commutative — order matters.
level3.explanationEs: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 se convierte en 3/4 × 2/1 = 6/4 = 1 1/2, mientras que 1/2 ÷ 3/4 se convierte en 1/2 × 4/3 = 4/6 = 2/3, así que las dos expresiones no son iguales. Intercambiar el dividendo y el divisor convierte el cociente en su recíproco, lo que muestra que la división no es conmutativa: el orden importa.
